A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DOLLAR study, with complete, readable main text and supplementary Sections 6–10. The equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments, VBench and diversity scores, runtime measurements, reward-tuning results, and human evaluations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original quantitative experiments, human evaluations, and qualitative video-generation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The combined VSD, generalized consistency distillation, and latent reward optimization method is unchanged. Section 3, Algorithm 1, and the appendix architectures retain the same procedures and objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same internal image/video training data and VBench evaluation coverage, including long and short prompts, human comparisons, and varied artistic styles and camera motions.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged in Table 2, the distillation and DDPO comparisons, and appendix examples. Although citations beside Gen-2 and Gen-3 are removed, both models remain in the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same training settings, 946 evaluation prompts with five videos each, and 128-frame outputs at 192 × 320 resolution. Sampling schedules, human-evaluation procedures, and DDPO gradient truncation also match.

E4.justification: The sampling-step, teacher-denoising-step, parameterization, prompt-length, and reward-overoptimization studies are retained unchanged. Appendix diversity analyses and qualitative case studies also match.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same mean and standard-deviation reporting for diversity, timing, and rewards, including Tables 3, 4, and 14. Sample counts and random-seed information are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains totals of 80.25 for the teacher, 82.37 for DOLLAR with PickScore, and 82.57 with HPSv2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, diversity formula, and DDPO derivations are unchanged. Supplementary Section 6 retains the same proofs of Equations 5 and 8.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about few-step quality, diversity, memory-efficient reward optimization, and up to 278.6-fold diffusion-sampling acceleration.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including prompt-length bias, reward overoptimization, residual diversity gaps, and disagreement between VBench and human preferences in supplementary Sections 8–9.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain the same, including eight A100 GPUs, up to 40,000 training iterations, optimizer settings, memory-saving techniques, and LRM architectures in Tables 12–13. The project-page access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes Esser et al.'s Structure-aware video generation with latent diffusion models, reference 10 in v1, and its citations in the abstract, related work, and baseline discussion. The remaining research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Citation callouts are removed or renumbered, and the arXiv version/date text changes. Substantive prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Minor reflow shifts paragraphs and existing displays within the main text; for example, the Diversity Measure heading moves from PDF page 9 to page 8. All 29 figures and 18 tables retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: The revision removes one reference and slightly reflows existing material. The experimental evidence, methods, reproducibility details, and substantive limitations remain unchanged across the main text and appendices. These localized editorial changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
